subject: Follow-up: Model fit & tool-calling evals for Finadata
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@finadata.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finadata.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Great call — next steps and eval asks

Thanks for the call today, Rishi — really helpful context on Redwood's routing and retry behaviors. A couple of asks from our side as we scope an initial POC: 

- Can you recommend the model family you think fits our use case (financial document extraction + structured output) and the trade-offs (latency/cost/quality)?
- Can you share any benchmark links or previous evals for structured-output / function-calling accuracy?
- We'll need a sample prompt set and expected JSON schema so engineering can validate parsing and downstream ingestion.

Also attaching the raw sample invoices and an initial prompt-set (attached IDs). Would appreciate a short mutual action plan and dates.

Thanks,
Olivia
Head of Data Platforms
Finadata

Attachments: finadata-sample-invoices.zip (attachment stub), prompt-set-v3.jsonl (attached)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@finadata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.j@finadata.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Great call — next steps and eval asks

Hi Olivia — thanks for the write-up and for sharing the samples. High level recommendations from our side: 

1) Recommended model family: For structured extraction with strict JSON schema compliance we usually start customers on the Redwood-2.7/structured variant (quantized if cost is a concern). It provides the best mix of deterministic structured output and reasonably low latency on our Dedicated pools. If you need the highest accuracy on edge-case financial language we can trial Redwood-7B-cx as a quality-focused variant.

2) Benchmarks & evals: Attached is our internal benchmark summary (redwood-benchmark-20261001.pdf) and a CSV showing precision/recall on your sample set we ran on Redwood-2.7 (finadata-eval-results.csv). Key notes: Redwood-2.7-structured hits ~92% schema-valid outputs on your invoice prompts with a 1.8% retry rate required for missing fields; Redwood-7B-cx increases schema-valid to ~96% but with 2-3x inference cost.

3) Tool/function calling & JSON schema: We validated function-calling flows for your invoice object schema. Best practice we recommend: 
- Provide a strict JSON Schema (we used the attached schema in the eval run).
- Configure the runtime to enable structured-output enforcement; for keys that are optional, include explicit null acceptance to avoid rejections.
- Use our retry-on-invalid-policy: two quick retries with slightly higher temperature (0.0 -> 0.2) and a final fallback to a strict parser when fields are missing.

Next steps / proposed MAP: 
- This week: share the final JSON Schema (we used a draft and attached prompt-set-v3.jsonl).
- 11/6: Redwood runs a 1k-record POC on your Dedicated test pool and shares full CSV of outputs + suggested prompt tweaks.
- 11/13: Joint review with engineering + CS to agree pass/fail criteria.

I've attached the benchmark and the per-record results we ran against your sample set. Looping in Marissa and Neha for the POC coordination and billing/contract side.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-20261001.pdf, finadata-eval-results.csv, prompt-set-v3.jsonl

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@finadata.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.j@finadata.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Great call — next steps and eval asks

Hi Olivia / Alex — quick note on POC logistics: 

- POC footprint: we'll reserve a small Dedicated test pool (1x A10G-equivalent) for the 1k-record run. If you prefer Hosted we can do that too but we'll need to size for peak concurrency.
- Data handling: uploads to our S3-compatible temp bucket; we retain POC artifacts for 14 days by default (can increase for audit).
- Procurement: Alex — can you confirm whether Finadata requires an MSA + SOW or if a short POC addendum will suffice? If you need an MSA, please loop procurement@finadata.com and we can get the legal team engaged.

I'll own scheduling and the run; Neha will handle product instrumentation so we can export token-level latency and error traces for each record.

Marissa
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

P.S. Two quick clarifications from our run: a) we observed a small class of failures where the model returned unexpected nested arrays for line_items — we added a post-process validation step in the eval (see notes in finadata-eval-results.csv). b) Our retry policy recovered ~60% of those failed records on the first retry (temp bump + system prompt tweak).

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finadata.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia@finadata.com>, procurement@finadata.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Great call — next steps and eval asks

Thanks — this is great context. Couple of quick items from procurement & engineering: 

- Procurement: we'll start with a POC addendum and preferred payment terms (Net 45). Please send the addendum template and a point of contact on legal.
- Engineering: can you confirm the exact JSON Schema you used (we need the $schema and explicit types for line_items.amount and date formats)? Also, if possible, can you include the exact request/response example for the retry-on-invalid-policy so our engineers can mirror it in our ingestion pipeline?

If you can send the addendum + schema by EOD Friday (11/6) we can get procurement to sign and the POC scheduled for 11/9.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Alex
Lead Platform Engineer
Finadata
